tasks.title: Keep service reports on the heartbeat cadence without overlap and preserve shutdown tracking
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify — Behavior (all bullets, implementing D1-D4 and R1-R8), Tests cases 1-7, and Completion evidence; Counterexamples 1-10, Performance impact, Security impact, and Acceptance evidence (feature). Keep the timer, shared report serializer and shutdown lifecycle together in startChannelLoop; add the regression tests before changing production code.

acceptance.expected: Red evidence, before changing src/index.ts: on unchanged main (the spec inspected 5a44c5a3de1764faa04b6cd3762f2c2be4c58430), case 1 passes with starts [0, 60000, 120000, 180000]; case 2 fails because actual starts [0, 60000, 124000] differ from the literal expected [0, 60000, 120000, 180000], with a 64000 ms gap. Record the command, actual lists and failing cases for the PR. A coverage-only failure does not establish the regression. Use the existing main dependency seams, a chronological injected clock/scheduler and injected fetch, isolated temporary state, and no external network or wall-clock sleeps standing for fake time. Keep production timeout wiring unchanged.

Green evidence after the fix: 7 pass, 0 fail; a focused run may fail only the global coverage threshold. Cases 1-2: poll 300000, latencies 0 and 4000, inclusive window [0, 180000], exact starts [0, 60000, 120000, 180000] and every adjacent gap <= 60000. Case 3: poll 54000, latency 4000, window [0, 100000], starts [0, 58000, 62000]; third body at equals its start (relative 62000). Case 4: poll 300000, hold the 60000 report across the ticks at 120000 and 180000 until release at 185000; all other reports have zero latency. Release, drain, then advance to 240000. Exact starts [0, 60000, 185000, 240000], exactly 4 reports; third body at equals its start (relative 185000). Reject a per-tick catch-up queue producing [0, 60000, 185000, 185000, 240000], old end-anchored timing producing [0, 60000], and skip producing [0, 60000, 240000]. Assert max in flight 1 in delayed, collision and held cases. Case 5: reject the 60000 report with TypeError; starts [0, 60000, 120000, 180000] and one service report failed warning. Case 6: stop at 1000 with only a pending timer, then advance to 300000; starts remain [0], no uncancelled channel timers and no added fetch. Case 7: poll 62000, hold the 60000 report, stop at 63000 with a poll report waiting; stop remains unresolved until release, then resolves with starts [0, 60000], no uncancelled channel timers and no added fetch after advancing to 300000. Assert complete start lists to reject missing reports, double arming and catch-up bursts.

All selected tests pass, 0 fail; a focused run may fail only the global coverage threshold. Both existing test files remain unchanged. Poll and heartbeat reports still occur, shutdown waits for an active beat and cancels the newest timer, and tokenless mode makes 0 service calls and 0 reports.

exit 0; lint, typecheck and the full test suite pass with at least 80% line coverage and cognitive complexity at most 15 per function. Existing report validation and integration coverage pass, including report-after-apply behavior. Do not weaken shared tooling or coverage settings.

acceptance.command: git diff --exit-code -- biome.json bunfig.toml eslint.config.js tsconfig.json .github src/service-report.ts src/api.ts src/ledger.ts src/config.ts test/index.test.ts test/channel-loop.review.test.ts
acceptance.expected: exit 0; all listed files remain unchanged from the implementation base. Report content, endpoint, ledger format 5, channel poll cadence, token handling, the 5000 ms service timeout and existing regression coverage remain intact.

acceptance.command: git diff --stat && git diff -- src/index.ts docs/channels.md
acceptance.expected: The complete implementation diff, including the added test once staged, contains only src/index.ts, test/report-heartbeat.test.ts and docs/channels.md. Review against D1-D4: the tick guards stopped/tokenless mode and arms only the next 60000 ms timer before requesting a report; settlement never arms a timer. Polls and beats share one in-flight report and one coalesced follow-up, whose body is built at its own start and whose waiters are released when shutdown drops it. Failures free the slot. Stop cancels the newest timer and awaits the running poll and active report before the existing ledger shutdown. The loop comment and channels documentation state start-anchored timing, no overlap and coalesced waiting.

Run on clean main and on the fixed branch with the same environment and dependency pins; both full suites pass. Record User time plus System time in seconds for each in the PR, as Performance impact requires. The spec expects test CPU to rise by well under 0.5 s; do not impose an invented performance threshold. Account separately for the runtime increase: at 4000 ms report latency heartbeat request rate rises by 6.7%, or 3.75 requests per hour; at the 5000 ms service timeout it rises by 8.3%, about 4.6 requests per hour and roughly 5 ms extra CPU per hour. These are the spec's estimates, not measured test CPU or a runtime gate. The local-API bench cannot exercise delayed reports; no bun bench/run.ts A/B is required.

Run on main and then on the fixed branch for 600 s of wall time each against the same local fake API, with a fixture service token and a fresh temporary state directory for each run. Keep the Bun.serve fake API script outside the repository: GET /service/notify/channels immediately returns a valid empty channel list, PUT /service/notify/report returns 204 after 4000 ms, and the server records each report arrival time. For each side record the report count, the complete list of gaps between report starts, and process CPU delta from utime + stime in /proc/<pid>/stat read right after start and at 600 s. Expected from Performance impact: main heartbeat gaps about 64 s; every branch gap at most 61 s, allowing 1 s wall-clock dispatch tolerance; branch heartbeat count equal to main or one greater. Observe no overlapping reports. Record the measured CPU difference, expected within the 10 ms resolution of /proc, without gating it. This delayed-report measurement also fulfills the required bun run start smoke run; stop cleanly and include the configured command and observed results in the PR without publishing the fixture token.

exit 0; review the diff against Security impact: no change to auth, parsing, HTTP headers or redirects, file writes, error/log text, dependencies, Dockerfile or CI. Record Security impact: no and the scope review in the PR.

exit 0; the PR CI check job passes lint, typecheck and tests, and both existing docker matrix jobs pass on ubuntu-24.04 and ubuntu-24.04-arm. No new compose end-to-end command is required by this section; notify has no compose test configuration.

The PR names issue #824 and includes the complete Completion evidence: baseline red command, failing cases and actual start lists; green command with all 7 cases passing, including the held-across-two-ticks starts [0, 60000, 185000, 240000]; successful bun run check and CI; unchanged tooling and protected files; scope limited to the three Files paths; measured main/branch test CPU seconds. Include both 600 s delayed-report bun run start commands and results: report counts, complete start-gap lists and process CPU deltas on main and the branch, comparison to about 64 s baseline gaps and branch gaps at most 61 s, and the observed CPU difference without a CPU threshold gate. Explain the spec's estimated heartbeat rate and runtime CPU increase when reports are slow. Include the security scope review and documented limits for runtime timer lateness and requests held longer than 60000 ms. Do not publish the fixture token.
